newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli fraud squad questions Netanyahu's lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Israeli fraud squad questions Netanyahu's lawyer.

text.p: An Israeli peacemaker who is also Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's lawyer appeared at Israel's police fraud unit on Tuesday to answer questions about alleged corruption in the appointment of an attorney-general.

"What I can tell you is that I came here to fulfill my civic duty to give testimony. What can I do?" the attorney, Yitzhak Molho, told reporters outside the national fraud unit in Jaffa near Tel Aviv.

Molho helped negotiate Israel's handover to the PLO of most of the West Bank town of Hebron. He was one of three attorneys to show up for questioning including Roni Bar-On, the man whose appointment by Netanyahu this month prompted the inquiry.
Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office, caught in a swirl of debate over his having got the job more for his loyalty to Netanyahu's Likud party than legal acumen.
A state-run television report then gave rise to charges his appointment was not just poor judgment but also criminal.

On Sunday, police launched an inquiry into the Channel One television report that Bar-On's appointment was part of a deal with Shas party leader Aryeh Deri, a political kingmaker on trial for corruption since 1993.
It said Deri, an ultra-Orthodox Jew and ex-cabinet minister, demanded Bar-On get the job in return for Shas party support for Netanyahu's accord with the PLO on Hebron, completed this month.

The television said that as part of the deal, Bar-On promised Deri a plea-bargain that would have enabled Deri to get on with his political career. The cabinet later approved the Hebron deal with Shas's support.
Bar-On, Deri and Netanyahu all denied the charges. Netanyahu, in office only seven months, demanded an inquiry.
